etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: ある (aru, “to be, to exist”, 連体形 (rentaikei) of the classical verb あり (ari)) + い (i, nominalizing suffix) + は (wa, topic marker). Arose from 漢文訓読 (kanbun kundoku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kaku/ → /kau/ → /kɔː/ → /koː/
Shift from 斯(か)く (kaku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *supu. Cognate with Okinawan 吸ぷゆん (shipuyun).
Likely an onomatopoeia. Compare Middle Korean ᄲᆞᆯ〮다〮 (spóltá, “to suck”), Middle Chinese 吸 (MC xip, “to suck”), Proto-Austronesian *-sep (“to suck”), Proto-Indo-European *sewg- (“to suck”), etc.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 命ずる (meizuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 塩(しお) (shio, “salt”) + 辛(から)い (karai, “harsh (of flavor); spicy, salty”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 字 (MC dziH).

etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨kuduru⟩ → /kuduru/ → /kud͡zuru/ → /kud͡zureru/
From Old Japanese 崩る (kuduru), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
First attested in the 播(はり)磨(ま)風(ふ)土(ど)記(き) (Harima Fudoki, “Harima Fudoki”) (715 CE).
Ultimately from 屑(くず) (kuzu, “rubbish, refuse, scrap, junk, waste”), and analyzable as etymologically meaning "to become rubbish". For the causative form 崩(くず)す (kuzusu), compare lay waste, ruin.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 州 (MC tsyuw).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 洲 (MC tsyuw). 州 is a daiyōji replacing 洲.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kazu apu/ → /kazo₁pu/ → /kazoɸu/ → /kazwoɸuru/ → /kazo(w)uru/ → /kazoweru/ → /kazoeru/
Inherited from Old Japanese.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 数ふ entry.
Equivalent to 数(かず) (kazu, “number”) + あう (au, “to join”). The earliest attestation of this verb uses the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん) (shimonidan, “lower bigrade”) conjugation pattern, suggesting an irregular shift from the 四(よ)段(だん) (yodan, “quadrigrade”) conjugation pattern of compounded verb あふ (afu, modern あう (au)). Compare the sporadic shift of the auxiliary verb ふ (-fu, expressing repetition or ongoing state) to える (-eru) in some terms.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: First appears in the late Edo period in a text from 1770. The clipped reading ほんと (honto) with the shorter second vowel is regarded as a simple shift from original reading ほんとう (hontō), and this first appears in a text from 1886.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Shift from ねぶる (neburu), from the same root with Old Japanese 寝 (nu) (whence 寝る (neru, “to sleep; to lie down”)), in turn from Proto-Japonic *naynpuru. Cognate with Kunigami 眠ん (ninbin /⁠níɴbîɴ⁠/), Northern Amami Ōshima 眠るり (nïbururi), Okinawan 眠じゅん (ninjun /⁠níɴdʑùɴ⁠/), Okinoerabu 眠ゆん (nibuyun /⁠nìbújúɴ⁠/), Southern Amami Ōshima 眠っゆむっ (nïpyum /⁠nɨ́pjùm̩⁠/), 眠りゅむっ (nïpryum /⁠nɨ́pɾʲùm̩⁠/), Tokunoshima 眠びゅい (ninbyui /⁠nɪ́ɴbʲúɪ́⁠/), Yoron 眠ゆん (nibuyun /⁠nìbùjùɴ⁠/), Miyako 眠ゔっ (niv), Yaeyama 眠ん (ninbun /⁠níbùɴ⁠/), and Yonaguni 眠どぅん (nindun /⁠níɴdúɴ⁠/).
Compare 眠い (nemui, “sleepy”), 眠たい (nemutai, “sleepy”), and おねむ (o-nemu, “(childish) sleepiness, sleep”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
First cited to the mid-800s.
From 膨, 脹 (fukura, “a bulge, a swelling”) + む (-mu, suffix indicating “looks like, seems like”). The fukura portion is in turn from now-archaic verb 膨る, 脹る (fukuru, “to swell, to bulge”), superseded by modern 膨れる, 脹れる (fukureru) of the same meaning.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 粗(あら)い (arai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨kapi₁⟩ → */kapʲi/ → /kaɸi/ → /kawi/ → /kai/
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *kapi. Appears voiced in the Kojiki of 712 CE in a compound, with the phonetic man'yōgana spelling 賀比, and in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Probably ultimately from Middle Chinese 貝 (MC pajH). Compare modern Min Nan pronunciation buê⁶, Cantonese bui³, Mandarin bèi.
First attested in 1284.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 連(つ)れる (tsureru, “to accompany, lead”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 連(つ)れ (tsure) by rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 避(さ)く (saku), cognate with Japanese 裂ける (sakeru). See the page for 避(さ)く (saku) for more information.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 部首 (MC buX syuwX). First mentioned in Chinese in the Shūowén Jiězì of roughly 100 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 順 (jun, “order”) + 序 (jo, “order”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From earlier 飽(あ)く (aku), irregularly evolved to kami ichidan conjugation.
